draft.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of knowing
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have many nations, each with its own languages, laws and ways of teaching. Learning is passed on over many generations and is not one single method.
Multimodal
knowledge is shared through more than one mode at once, such as story, song, dance, art and hands-on practice. Learners watch, listen, take part and do.
Connected to Country
Country includes land, waters, sky and the living things and ancestors linked to a place. Learning about plants, seasons and law happens on Country, so knowledge is tied to a particular place.
Relationships
Knowledge is shared within relationships, such as between Elders and young people. Who teaches and who learns depends on kinship, community roles and responsibilities.
draft.remember: Learning is shared through many modes, on Country, and within relationships.

a.q: Which description best fits Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of knowing?
opts: Knowledge is shared through story, song and practice in place
Knowledge is recorded in one written form and studied alone
Knowledge is learned only by trial and error in a classroom
Knowledge is the same in every nation and place
a.why: Learning is multimodal and tied to Country, so story, song and practice are used together in place. The written, solo option is wrong because knowledge is shared within relationships, and the last option is wrong because each nation has its own knowledge.
a.clue: Think of learning that uses many modes and happens in place.

b.q: An Elder takes young people onto Country and teaches them about the seasons through a story, a song and by showing them how to gather food. Which feature of learning does this show most clearly?
opts: It is multimodal, using several modes together on Country
It uses one mode, because the story carries all the learning
It is separate from place, so it can be taught anywhere
It depends on a fixed test to show what was learned
b.why: The Elder uses story, song and practice together, which is multimodal, and does so on Country, linking knowledge to place. Saying one mode carries it all is tempting because story is central, but the card says several modes are used at once.
b.clue: Count how many ways the Elder shares the knowledge, and where.
